target_customer: Hospitality operators, landowners and consumers buying flat-pack off-grid shelters; early pitch also covered disaster relief
problem: Putting temporary or off-grid lodging on land is slow and expensive because of permitting, construction and utility hookups.
business_model: Hardware sales of flat-pack shelters plus planning services for landowners

founders.name: Jeff Wilson
founders.background_notes: The seed press release describes him as a former environmental science professor who lived in a dumpster for a year as an experiment.

founders.name: Antonio Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: Press release says he led a 100 million dollar sprinter van conversion business at OYO and served on an advisory board to the National Park Service.

technical_complexity.rationale: Flat-pack insulated shelters with prewired solar and battery systems need hardware design and manufacturing, but the product was a structure rather than a new technology.

defensibility.rationale: Designs were copyable by other prefab and glamping pod makers. The brand and design were the main differentiators, supported by press coverage.

market_need_then: The seed release frames demand around temporary and mobile housing and off-grid lodging listed on Airbnb and Hipcamp. Dwell and Futurism coverage showed consumer pre-orders at 17,500 dollars per unit in 2020.

identity.visual_style: Space-themed design described by Dezeen in December 2020 and by Product Hunt as inspired by the stars and 2001: A Space Odyssey.
identity.voice_and_tone: Just Add Land tagline, a simple promise.

branding.brand_signature: Just Add Land tagline, registered as a trademark filing in March 2022
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Dezeen, Dwell, Futurism, Yahoo and Business Insider, and the founder appeared on a podcast.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong design press for a seed stage hardware company and a memorable tagline, but no evidence of community or fan activity.

pivots.to: Hospitality shelters and land activation services
pivots.why: Only a job-board summary and the current site describe the shift; no founder statement found.

outcome_analysis: Jupe raised a 9.5 million dollar seed in December 2021 and drew strong design press, but YC lists it as Inactive while the company site is still live with a hospitality focus. A job board summary says Jon Leonardo acquired it in 2023 and refocused it on land activation, which would explain the mismatch but rests on one aggregator. No shutdown cause is public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Seed confirmed by the press release and by Pulse 2.0, a second outlet. Totals conflict: Simplify says 11.6M across 3 rounds, CB Insights about 9.63M, and one report says roughly 1M pre-seed plus 3M at Demo Day before a 4.5M seed. Those earlier rounds are not recorded because no dated source was opened. The 2023 acquisition by Jon Leonardo rests on a single job board and is not recorded as an exit. YC lists status Inactive but jupe.com is live with a 2026 copyright, so the exit type is unknown. No dated competitor source was found; Dezeen and Dwell articles cover Jupe itself.
